chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to him, saying: Yaqoob ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Maysami, from al-Muthanna al-Han'nat, who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:
The days of God, the Mighty and Exalted, are three: the Day when the Riser rises, the Day of Return, and the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الْكُرَّةُ: The Return (resurrection of souls before bodily resurrection)

ai.seo_question: What are the three days of God mentioned in Shia eschatology?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three pivotal moments as the primary markers of divine intervention, distinguishing the Mahdi's emergence and the Resurrection (al-Kurrah) from the final Judgment. This classification underscores the eschatological framework in Shia thought, where the appearance of the Qa'im initiates the era of justice preceding the ultimate accountability of humanity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-75 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Maysami, on the authority of Masni al-Han’nat that he had heard Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB) say,
“The days of the Honorable the Exalted God are three: the Day on which the Riser (MGB) shall rise; the Day of Return and the Resurrection Day.”
